result.summary: Three supported Desktop preview/apply defects remain. Pinned evidence digests and bundled protocol integrity match; selected read-only core/preload checks pass. Full verification and independent formal Judge remain required.

criteria.explanation: Schema-1 compatibility remains intact; schema-2 ordering is retained separately from module definitions.
evidence: cli/test/owner-ordering.test.js:20 — compatibility and round-trip check passed during this review.

criteria.explanation: Policy resolution rejects malformed relationships, invalid endpoints, protected duplicates, cross-slot links and active combined cycles before mutation.
evidence: cli/test/owner-ordering.test.js:33 — negative checks passed during this review.

criteria.explanation: Owner edges require enabled endpoints; saved relationships survive disabling, while locked modules and hard prerequisites remain enforced.
evidence: cli/test/owner-ordering.test.js:49 — endpoint enablement checks passed during this review.

criteria.explanation: Compiled owner dependencies participate in eligibility and predecessor-event freshness without imposing global barriers.
Migration detects ordering changes, retains historical graphs and keeps ordering-only predecessors outside Judge evidence inputs.
Dependency absorption omits staged ordering from its follow-up preview, and pending responses can overwrite discarded draft state.
Discard does not cancel pending previews, and Apply can confirm and submit edits whose current preview has not completed.
Individual-edge rendering is implemented, but dependency absorption can supply the preview with saved edges instead of the staged combined graph.
Named textual relationships distinguish edge origins, and derived layout explicitly explains that rows impose no completion barrier.
Canonical and bundled protocol files match, projection hashes validate, and supplied logs report portable and regression checks passing. Full verification remains pending.
evidence: apps/desktop/resources/desktop-projection.json:4 — protocol hash and listed file digests independently matched.
apps/desktop/resources/protocol/modules.js:120 — bundled protocol files are byte-identical to canonical sources.

scopeCheck.explanation: All 33 inventoried changes concern the approved policy, graph, Desktop, documentation or regression-test scope. Document, inventory, patch-chunk and changed-source identities match. No binary changes are inventoried.

gapCheck.explanation: The supplied renderer coverage waits for completed previews; it misses ordering combined with dependency absorption, Discard during pending requests and Apply during pending validation. Read-only execution of the source functions reproduced these gaps.

contradictionCheck.explanation: The implementation can display one policy and migration impact while submitting another, contradicting the approved accurate-preview and stale-apply requirements.

findings.summary: Dependency absorption previews saved ordering while Apply submits staged ordering.
findings.invariant: Every preview and migration disclosure must describe the complete staged policy that Apply will submit.
evidence: apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1320 — the first preview includes moduleDraftOrdering.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1333 — after auto-enabling prerequisites, the second preview omits ordering.
apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:104 — omitted ordering falls back to committed policy.

Read-only source-function reproduction: staging Judge after Code Review and enabling a module with an auto-enabled prerequisite produced a displayed preview with ordering={} while the draft retained the owner edge. Staged removals of saved edges are likewise previewed incorrectly.

findings.summary: Pending previews can restore changes after Discard.
findings.invariant: Discard must invalidate outstanding draft requests so their responses cannot restore discarded state.
evidence: apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:3028 — Discard resets drafts and preview without advancing modulePreviewRequest.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1321 — the pending response therefore passes its request-generation check.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1331 — dependency absorption can replace the restored enabled IDs with discarded IDs.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1336 — an ordinary pending response can restore discarded ordering disclosure and re-enable Apply.

Read-only delayed-response reproduction: Discard restored committed enabled IDs; releasing a pending dependency preview re-staged the discarded child and parent modules. A pending ordering-only response also restored its discarded preview while ordering controls remained reset.

findings.summary: Apply can confirm newer ordering edits against an older preview.
findings.invariant: Apply and migration confirmation must be bound to the latest completed validation of the exact submitted draft.
evidence: apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1205 — ordering controls immediately mutate the draft and start asynchronous validation.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1315 — refresh leaves the previous valid preview and enabled Apply button in place while awaiting IPC.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1383 — confirmation displays the previous preview's migration impact.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1397 — submission reads the newer mutable draft.

Read-only delayed-response reproduction: while the displayed preview contained only Judge after Code Review, Apply remained enabled and submitted an additional Code Review after Pattern Review edge with confirmedMigration=true before its preview completed.
